tooltip.title: The Immune Basis of Psoriasis
tooltip.markdown: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated disease where an interplay of genetic and environmental factors triggers a cascade of inflammation, primarily driven by the IL-23/Th17 axis.

tooltip.title: Genetic & Environmental Factors
tooltip.markdown: The initial phase where susceptibility meets a trigger, initiating the inflammatory process.

tooltip.title: Genetic Susceptibility
tooltip.markdown:
-   **HLA-C\*06:02:** The main genetic risk factor for psoriasis.
-   **HLA-B\*27:** A strong genetic marker for axial disease in Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA).
-   **Other Genes:** Loci related to IL23R and other immune pathways are also implicated.

tooltip.title: Environmental Triggers
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Infections:** Streptococcal pharyngitis is a classic trigger for guttate psoriasis.
-   **Trauma (Koebner):** Psoriatic lesions appearing at sites of skin injury.
-   **Stress:** Both physical and psychological stress can trigger or exacerbate psoriasis.
-   **Medications:** Beta-blockers, lithium, and antimalarials are known triggers.

tooltip.title: The IL-23/Th17 Axis
tooltip.markdown: The core inflammatory pathway driving the clinical manifestations of psoriasis.

tooltip.title: Antigen-Presenting Cells (APCs)
tooltip.markdown: Dendritic cells in the skin are activated by triggers and produce key cytokines, including IL-23 and IL-12.

tooltip.title: Th17 Cell Activation
tooltip.markdown: IL-23 acts as a "master cytokine" that promotes the survival and proliferation of Th17 cells. These cells are the primary source of IL-17. \[1\]

tooltip.title: Effector Cytokines (IL-17 & IL-22)
tooltip.markdown:
-   **IL-17:** A key pro-inflammatory cytokine that stimulates keratinocytes to produce chemokines, recruiting inflammatory cells (like neutrophils) into the skin.
-   **IL-22:** Directly drives the hyperproliferation of keratinocytes, leading to the thick, scaly plaques characteristic of psoriasis. \[1\]
-   **TNF-α:** Another critical cytokine that contributes to the overall inflammatory milieu.

tooltip.title: Clinical Manifestation
tooltip.markdown: The result of the cytokine cascade on the skin.

tooltip.title: Plaque Formation
tooltip.markdown:
The combined effects of IL-17 and IL-22 lead to:

-   **Hyperproliferation:** Epidermal cell turnover is dramatically increased.
-   **Inflammation:** Influx of neutrophils and other immune cells into the epidermis and dermis.
-   **Vascular Changes:** Dilation of blood vessels in the dermis.

This results in the characteristic erythematous, indurated, and scaly psoriatic plaque.
